pages.description: Limp vellum front cover, blank. No drawing.
Inside front cover with modern library pastedown, bookplate and shelf notes. No original drawing.

Text-only opening page: four paragraphs with red/rubricated initials in the left margin. Faint green leaf-shaped stains are show-through or offset, not a drawing. Likely an introduction, prologue or table of contents rather than a single plant.

Shrub with forked woody stems with knobby nodes; alternate elliptic pointed leaves coloured alternately green and tan/brown; a single white cup-shaped flower or calyx at the top holding a dark brown round berry; a large crosshatched lumpy root mass. A dark berry sitting in a pale calyx suggests deadly nightshade or another Solanaceae.

Three thistle-like flower heads with fringed pale-brown florets on bracteate green involucres dotted red; narrow, palmately/pinnately cut leaves; red-lined stems; red branched root. A knapweed / cornflower / centaury type (Centaurea-like composite).

One huge round, kidney-shaped green leaf with a deep basal notch on a long stem; a small trumpet/bell-shaped white flower with a green calyx at the top; base a strip of small round pebble-like tubercles (perhaps water bed or bulbils). Water lily, asarabacca, pennywort or bindweed type.

Single erect stalk ending in a dense oblong head of stacked wavy crescent bands, alternating green and red, with dotted edges and pointed tips; two broad leaves at the base of the head; fibrous red-brown root bundle. Possibly a coloured-leaf rosette (beet/chard, amaranth/cockscomb), a fern frond, or a palm/aloe drawn schematically.

Stem with six deeply cut claw/star-shaped leaves on curling stalks; two nodding dark blue flower heads (hood-like) each with a pale yellow crosshatched disc or seed face; long segmented reddish root with ring nodes ending in a hook. Monkshood/aconite, hellebore, love-in-a-mist or larkspur type.

Bushy herb: many upright branches densely set with small narrow paired leaves coloured green and red; small pale nodding bell/tubular flowers at branch tips and a small umbel-like cluster at the top; fine fibrous root. Heath, flax, toadflax, St John's wort, centaury, thyme or hyssop type.

Dark blue bell/tulip-shaped flower at the top with green star-shaped bracts above and below; spiky star-like whorls on the stem; arching branches with crescent narrow leaves; brown two-knobbed tuberous root with rootlets. Gentian, bellflower or columbine type.

Single stalk through a large rosette of broad, overlapping rounded green leaves (cabbage/umbrella-like); small white flower with drooping petals and a dark crown on top; thin roots with small dotted tubers. Cabbage, mandrake, coltsfoot, plantain or a broad-leaved rosette herb.

Branching herb with palmately lobed, toothed leaves; small red five-petalled flowers with dark blue sepals and nodding buds; tuberous brown root. Crane's-bill/geranium, herb Robert, mallow or avens type.

Erect stem with three large pinnately lobed leaves with long finger-like lobes near the base; four club/sac-shaped green pods or bladders curving outward, each ending in a red-rimmed open mouth fringed with hairs; twisted, rope-like intertwined roots. Fern-leaved plant with odd pods: acanthus, a fern, a thistle, or a poppy/henbane capsule drawing.

Plant with deeply palmate star-shaped leaves (5-7 points); round spiny burr-like fruits, green centres ringed in dark blue, bristly, at the top and one on the stem; fibrous root. Castor oil plant, chestnut burr, burdock or thorn-apple type.

Single stem bearing a giant eight-pointed star rosette of long narrow green leaves with inner pale pinkish striped petal-like leaves; simple forked red root. Star-shaped flower or leaf rosette: star-of-Bethlehem, saffron/crocus, squill, lily or aloe.

Basal rosette of oval leaves with hairy/ciliate edges, each marked with a dark blue spot; two leaves on the stem coloured red; tall bare stem with three small dark berries or buds at the top; small tapering root. Spotted leaves strongly suggest lungwort; also spotted persicaria or hound's-tongue.

One tall thin stem with a single large triangular, arrow-shaped (hastate) green leaf at the top and a small lens-shaped leaf lower; text wraps around; branching root with one rootlet ending in a dot. Arum/cuckoo-pint, birthwort, ivy, sorrel, dock or bindweed leaf.

Erect leafy stem with ovate pointed leaves; tubular flowers red at the tip, emerging from dark blue striped calyces; spreading brown root. Pink/carnation type, or a borage-family plant whose flowers turn red to blue (comfrey, bugloss, lungwort).

Rosette of roundish crinkled, lobed leaves on red petioles from a thick crown; tall red stem with spike-like clusters of tiny red-brown dotted seeds/flowers; large carrot-like tapered root with hairs and crosshatching. Rhubarb, dock, sorrel, lovage or celery type.

Five-petalled flowers, blue-violet with some yellow lower petals (two-toned, pansy-like); narrow toothed leaves and narrow cut stipules along the stem; fibrous root. Very likely heartsease / wild pansy or another violet.

Leafy erect stem with paired toothed ovate leaves, some green and some olive-brown (wilting), curving down; on a long arching stalk a single radiating blue flower with fringed blue ray florets around a pale yellow oval centre, with a pale bud; horizontal roots ending in two red oval tubers. Cornflower, chicory or scabious type.

Stem with paired, wavy, twisting strap-like dark green leaves; two nodding dark blue bell flowers on arching stalks; tuberous rhizome root with pointed rootlets. Bluebell/hyacinth, Solomon's seal, bellflower or monkshood type.

Dense rounded crown of overlapping scalloped green leaves studded with small dark blue trumpet-shaped flowers; three pale stems arising from three hairy/spiny brownish sheaths that cross; long spiky, hairy roots. Rosemary, lavender, hyssop or a blue-flowered shrublet.

Tree-like plant: a dense ovoid crown of overlapping scale-like leaves coloured green and russet/brown (like a pine cone, artichoke or hop cone); a blue fan-shaped tuft or flower on top; trunk of many fine red-lined stems; root cluster of cut stubs with fibrous roots. Pine cone, cypress, juniper, artichoke or hop.

Broad rounded, scalloped/notched leaves on long petioles, half green and half olive-brown; central stalk with a dense club-shaped cluster of pale pod-like buds topped with white dotted tips, the uppermost blue; bulbous red-brown twisted root/corm ringed with white knobs at the crown. Butterbur/coltsfoot (round leaves plus a club flower spike), cyclamen, beet or rhubarb.

Two stems from one brown root, each with a cylindrical/conical stack of overlapping scale-leaves (green and olive, like an artichoke or cabbage head); the left topped by three dark blue elongated buds with recurved white sepals, the right by a further leafy head. Artichoke/cardoon, cabbage, houseleek or columbine.

Tall stalk with whorls of long narrow, pointed, sword-like leaves on red petioles and red stem; single small red-orange star flower over a dark green oval bud/fruit on top; base of two pale sheathing stems on a large coiled, ring-segmented horizontal rhizome (snake-like). Iris/flag, gladiolus or sweet flag (calamus).

Two large spiky-edged, comb-like serrated leaf fans; three stalks with curled pale crozier-like clusters of dotted (seed-filled) flowers with blue dots, like scorpioid cymes; red-brown cross-shaped root with cut-end stubs. Heliotrope (scorpion's-tail), borage-family, fern with sori, thistle or teasel.

Stem with oak-leaf-like lobed pinnate leaves, each leaf tip trailing a chain of pale bead/bulbil-like swellings; two long pale vase-shaped capsules or buds with blue-dotted tips; one radiating sunburst flower (fine rays around a pale golden oval disc) at the top; red sheath and red spreading root. Poppy (capsule plus sunburst), salsify/goat's-beard (pappus clock), dandelion or a bulbil-bearing herb.

Four broad rounded, spade-shaped leaves with curled tips in a cross on a stem; a tall pale stalk ending in a white elongated spathe-like bulb from which a long curled crest of pale yellow drop-shaped florets hangs; fibrous root. Herb Paris (four leaves in a cross), an arum, or lily-of-the-valley type.

Palmately compound leaves with many narrow toothed leaflets (hemp-like); at the top a dense spike of curled clusters of tiny red and white dotted flowers among small green bracts; thick pale root with finger-like hairy lobes. Hemp, hop or chaste tree.

One large blue/teal star flower with fringed bracts and four pale elongated petals round a yellow dotted central disc (sea-holly-like); four red jagged sunburst flowers with toothed dark red rays and pale leafy centres; pale brown sheath-like root. Sea holly/eryngo, carline thistle, or a pomegranate/pink-flowered plant.

Erect stem with long narrow, ladder-like paired leaves; three dark blue-black brush/thistle-like flower heads with pale fringed tips on green cups; fibrous root marked with two red diamonds. A faint later marginal note runs along the top edge. Globe thistle, knapweed, scabious or cornflower type.

Climbing vine: long trailing stem with a spiral tendril at left; bunches of red berries along the top; alternate ovate pointed toothed leaves; long hairy jointed brown root, like a segmented hairy rhizome. Bryony (tendrils, red berries, huge root), black bryony, bittersweet nightshade or hop.

Upright stem with smooth spoon-shaped leaves; terminal flower with dark blue ray petals around a red-dotted centre; small white buds with red tips in the leaf axils; fibrous root. Chicory, aster, marigold or blue daisy type.

Branching stem with groups of rounded, deeply lobed leaflets (celandine/buttercup/parsley-like); at the top a large round flower head with a fringed, hairy outer ring, a cup of overlapping scales and a pale blue-grey disc bearing a cluster of red berries; root a thick bulb with a long horizontal branching fleshy rhizome with many finger-like shoots. Celandine, buttercup, strawberry, avens or wood anemone.

Two large drooping comb-like (pectinate) arching fronds at the base; an erect stem with smaller toothed narrow leaves; several small blue-and-white cone/cluster buds; one large dark blue three-petalled, lily-like flower with a tan fringed edge on a green leafy cup at the top; pale root crown flaring into fibrous roots. Iris, larkspur, a fern with flower, or spiderwort type.

Tall pale stem from a red-brown bulbous root with spreading roots; two tiers of dense, fringed, spiky green brush-like foliage on whorled stalks; three long thin stalks at the top each with a small blue three-lobed bud over a pale oval capsule. Horsetail, fennel/dill (feathery foliage), asparagus, leek/onion (bulb plus capsule) or flax.

Low bushy herb with pinnate leaves of many small oval leaflets (legume-like); upright racemes with red/pink pod- or keel-shaped flowers and small dark blue buds at the tips; small fibrous root. Vetch, liquorice, sainfoin, goat's-rue or milk-vetch.

Stem with bands of long narrow grass-like leaves held in clasping bundles; many umbel-like flower heads on long stalks, each a pale fringed cup with a dark blue cap or capsule; root mostly cut off at the bottom of the page. Chives/leek or another allium, rush, flax capsules, scabious or cornflower.

Low spreading, radiating bush: many branches with tiny round paired leaves and chains of small tan/brown bead-like flowers or seed clusters along them; faint roots. Wild thyme, knotgrass, stonecrop, chickweed, rupturewort or heather type.

Stem with pinnate leaves drawn as rows of crescent-shaped green leaflets with white gaps; branched top with many funnel/trumpet flowers, dark blue with red-tipped teeth/stamens; small brown loop-shaped root. Larkspur, bugloss, gentian, or a pinnate-leaved blue-flowered herb (goat's-rue, woad, liquorice).

Upright stem forking from a split pale base; side leaves rounded with pale scalloped inner halves; at the top a dense candelabrum of many erect red-and-white beaded catkin- or spike-like racemes; above them three dark blue-black hanging globes (berries/fruits); red fibrous roots. Bistort or persicaria (red spikes), dock seed spikes, sumac, elder or currant.

Stem with five fan-shaped leaves, each a bundle of parallel striped (green/yellow/white) segments ending in a broad scalloped green lobe; a single large closed oval flower bud at the top with yellow and blue scales at its tip; horizontal thorny red-brown rhizome with chain links/rings and many vertical rootlets. Thistle or artichoke bud, rose/bramble (thorny root), acanthus or tulip-like bulb.

Two stems from a long horizontal jointed, log-like rhizome with cut ends and many rootlets; palmate, hand-shaped leaves with 5-7 round-toothed fingers; small clusters of blue five-petalled rosette flowers at the top. Cinquefoil, lady's mantle, hellebore, sanicle, or a blue-flowered plant such as periwinkle or forget-me-not.

Tall pale stem from a branching red root; clusters of broad roundish leaves with hairy/fringed edges, green and olive-brown mixed; a large top flower with eight narrow blue petals round a large pale ringed centre, and two small dark blue star flowers on side branches. Borage (hairy leaves, blue star flowers), bugloss or comfrey.

Two twisted, intertwined stems with many short-stalked rounded heart/cup-shaped leaves; each stem ends in a large green hooded leaf/spathe holding a white daisy-like flower with many rounded petals and an oval golden centre; long wavy roots. Chamomile, daisy, feverfew or ox-eye daisy; possibly a water lily.

Stem with paired, rounded leaves each drawn like a comma or tadpole (round blade with a long tapering point); five dark blue fringed, carnation/cornflower-like flowers in pale cupped calyces at the top; root a cluster of red-brown spindle-shaped tubers. Cornflower/pink type flowers; spindle tubers suggest dropwort, lesser celandine or asphodel.

Single thin stem with opposite pairs of broad ovate, softly toothed leaves and a crowded terminal tuft; small red-brown flower or bud pairs at the leaf nodes; thin red branching root. Nettle (small axillary flowers), mint, dead-nettle, dog's mercury, pellitory or balm.

Large star-shaped rosette of long lanceolate, pointed leaves radiating from a short stem; pale reddish fibrous root; at lower right a small upright dragon/lizard-like creature with ears or crest and a long tail on a green stalk, facing the plant. The creature may be a name pun: dragon arum, dragonwort or tarragon (dracunculus), or a snake-root.

Stem with roundish wavy-edged, scalloped leaves on stalks; two long forking upper stems each ending in a cluster of small dark blue berries or buds on short pedicels; red root splitting into strands. Bilberry, black nightshade, blackcurrant, elder, ivy berries or grape hyacinth.

Tree or shrub with pinnate fronds of many rounded leaflets drawn as rows of green lumps; at the top a cluster of many cup-shaped fruits: pale dotted cups with blue-black caps, acorn-like; red tangled roots. Oak with acorns, ash, sumac, elder, rowan or walnut.

Two plants. Main: a cluster of large broad, lanceolate, parallel-veined leaves on a single stem; two small dark blue-black fringed flower cups and a small leafy sprig at the top; forked root. Secondary small plant at lower right: three round scalloped leaves on a forked stem with fibrous root. White hellebore, ramsons, lily-of-the-valley, plantain or Solomon's seal; the small plant suggests ground ivy, pennywort or moneywort.

Shrubby herb with arching branches of serrated, pinnately arranged leaflets; long pale flower stalks with small radiating starburst flowers (fine white rays round a red centre) and pairs of curled blue buds; pale lumpy root with brown patches. Valerian, agrimony, elder, feverfew/chamomile or a pimpernel-like star flower.

Long pale pinkish stem piercing a large pinwheel whorl of wavy green leaves with curled tips; three segmented, ribbed, cocoon-like cones stacked on the stem, the topmost with a yellow cap and a red berry; red bulbous root with tentacle-like branches. Horsetail (whorls plus segmented cone), mullein spike or plantain spike.

Stem with two opposite leaves; above, a large circular wreath of about sixteen wavy, narrow green leaflets or flame-like segments on fine stalks round an empty centre, with a small spike at its base; pale tuberous root with fingers. Whorled-leaved plant (woodruff, madder, cleavers), herb Paris, or a seed-head 'clock'.

Stem rising from a fan of broad, arching, overlapping hood-like leaves coloured green, olive and slate blue (cabbage/kale-like); at the top an elongated dotted cylindrical spike with a red-rimmed opening at its tip; below it a cluster of five red berries over a fringed cup; roots drawn as straight radiating lines spreading horizontally. Arum / cuckoo-pint (spadix plus red berries) or cabbage/kale.

Pair of spreading, arching comb-toothed olive leaves at the base; tall stalks bearing many green urn/tulip-shaped spiky-tipped buds or capsules, the topmost opening dark blue with petals; thick horizontal rhizome with comb-like rootlets. Thistle, teasel, larkspur/monkshood (blue spiky buds), columbine or love-in-a-mist.

Two clumps of lanceolate leaves (lower and middle) on a thin stem with a fibrous root; a curved, arching one-sided raceme of small hanging dark blue bell flowers. Lily-of-the-valley form in blue: bluebell/wild hyacinth, grape hyacinth, Solomon's seal or bellflower.

Stem with paired olive-brown ovate serrated leaflets (pinnate); top two curling forked stalks lined with small round yellowish-tan knobs on short stalks (seed/berry-like); wavy horizontal brown root. Agrimony (toothed pinnate leaves plus burr fruits along a spike), moonwort or a fern, barberry or elder.

Stout erect stem with a few very large, broad, crumpled dark green leaves low down; several pale composite flower heads (yellowish fringed discs with scaly cups) at the top and on side branches; a huge long red-brown horizontal root branching into many rootlets at both ends. Burdock or elecampane (big leaves, composite heads, massive root); also butterbur or comfrey.

Odd plant: a block of stacked chevron/zigzag green leaves with a lower band of brown (withered) leaves; a long stalk with a round head covered in small dots/circles and fine radiating lines (a seed or umbel head); two side stalks with green leafy calyx cups holding dark blue-black ovoid fruits; long straight thin roots. Allium umbel (onion/leek/garlic), poppy head, or a nightshade with black berries in calyces.

Branching stem with alternate ovate, smooth-edged leaves; four or five dense rounded flower heads of small white flowers spotted blue, each topped with yellow star-like tufts; horizontal green ground lines at the base. Self-heal, bugle, oregano/marjoram, basil, calamint or betony type (labiate).

Stem with many small star-shaped five-pointed (ivy/maple-like) leaves on side shoots; three large dark blue trumpet/funnel flowers with pale calyx tubes and protruding stamens, plus smaller pale buds at the top; thick pale root with lateral rootlets, brown at the crown. Columbine (palmate leaves plus blue flowers), bellflower, bindweed/morning glory, monkshood or larkspur.

Bushy plant with ovate pointed, slightly toothed leaves; two large pale green ribbed, speckled urn-shaped calyces (inflated) crowned by round radiating discs (green striped petals around a ring of small seeds/stamens), plus a smaller bud; orange-brown root spreading horizontally and ending left and right in drawn faces or animal heads. Henbane (urn calyx, lidded seed capsule), mandrake (faces on the root), poppy or bladder campion.

Two huge oval flower heads drooping on long stalks: a ring of dark blue heart-shaped florets round an oval yellow centre packed with seeds in rows; below, star-shaped, deeply lobed green and olive leaves in whorls; root with three round brown radial structures (like cut root slices, seed pods or spoked wheels) at the tips. Composite with big seed disc: globe/carline thistle, artichoke/cardoon, teasel; root discs might be cut tubers.

Tall stem with broad fan- or hand-shaped leaves with fringed, jagged tips; three nodding flower heads, each a green fringed cup holding a blue scaly oval centre; pink-orange root with many flat strap-like roots. Thistle/scabious/knapweed heads; palmate leaves with nodding heads might also suggest hellebore.

Tree or shrub: branching limbs bearing many round fruits set in fluted, ribbed cups, coloured green, brown, red-brown (various ripeness); three pale scaly cone- or artichoke-like buds at the top; a great spreading orange root tangle with a central oval 'eye'. Fruits in cups strongly suggest oak with acorns or hazelnut; also chestnut, medlar, quince or fig.

A single huge cup- or goblet-shaped leaf or bract (olive-brown body with fringed green upper edge, like a calyx or spathe) on a red-lined stem; from its top a stalk with a flower of blue curled, hooked petals round a red-and-white striped centre; root of two pale ribbed spreading lobes. Columbine or aconite flower over an arum-like spathe; or a tulip/lily cup.

Tall pale green stem with two thinner stems twisting round it like a vine; dense lobed, scalloped green crown at the top; a few separate deeply lobed, oak-like leaves; many clusters of 3-6 small round blue-green berries (one cluster dark red) on short stalks; long red-brown sprawling horizontal roots. Climbing vine with berry clusters: ivy, grape vine, hop, bryony or juniper.

Herb with many long-stalked, deeply lobed, crinkled leaves (some coloured pale yellow, as if dried); slender upper stems with small pale dotted seed capsules and tiny blue and yellow five-petalled flowers; thick crown with knotted brown claw-like roots. Greater celandine, crane's-bill, fumitory, buttercup, mugwort/wormwood or a horned poppy.

Erect stem with many palmate, star-like leaves of 6-9 narrow rounded leaflets (lupin/hemp/cinquefoil-like) on stalks; at the top and in leaf axils, curled pale brown catkin- or cone-like clusters of small scaly/beaded flowers (like hop cones or seed spikes); red-brown root with many parallel rootlets like a comb. Lupin, hop, hemp, cinquefoil or lady's mantle.

Tall stem with long drooping lanceolate leaves in pairs (willowherb/ smartweed-like); at the top branched clusters of round berry-like heads made of many small red-and-white beads (like raspberry/mulberry or clustered flowers); brown forked root. Bramble/raspberry, mulberry, persicaria, sorrel/dock seed clusters, or elder.

Single pale stem with paired, rounded, scalloped leaves that get larger toward the base (curved crescent/cup shapes); top three dark blue oblong buds or fruits, two capped with small red-and-white flowers; thick dark brown branching root. Comfrey, hound's-tongue, mullein, foxglove-like rosette, or a borage-family plant.

One huge green feather/arrow-shaped leaf (V-shaped notch at top, comb-toothed edges) marked with five white comma/tadpole spots; a reddish stem with two pale vase-shaped sheaths at the leaf base; near the root two pale trumpet-shaped buds or fruits on stalks; red fibrous root. Fern (spleenwort/hart's-tongue), spotted-leaf arum, or a palm-like frond.

Tall column-shaped crown of overlapping diamond/rhombic leaves in green, olive-brown and pale blue-grey, like scales or a stacked hedge; a small dark blue star flower (8 rays) at the top right; thin red-striped trunk; spreading brown root. Cypress or juniper (columnar), stonecrop/houseleek column, or a cornflower-topped plant.

A row of about ten separate shoots, each with two or three broad lanceolate leaves speckled with small dark dots, growing from a long flat oval root plate with many hanging roots; one shoot carries a tall dark blue tubular/bell flower topped by a yellow five-petalled flower. Spotted leaves suggest lungwort or spotted orchid; the row form suggests a colony (ramsons, lily-of-the-valley); blue tube flower suggests gentian.

Rosette of long, strap-like dark green leaves with wavy lobed edges and white notches/holes along the midrib; two tall stalks each ending in a rounded umbel/cluster of small blue and white star (5-8 petalled) flowers; thick root stub with red-striped spreading roots. Blue umbel flowers suggest borage-family (forget-me-not, hound's-tongue), scabious, or an allium; leaves like dandelion/chicory.

Stem with fan-shaped leaves cut into many narrow comb-like fingers, arranged in pairs on curved stalks; at the top a tall pale spindle-shaped vase/capsule with an olive-green band and blue streaks, crowned with a round blue daisy-like flower (many petals round a pale dotted centre); long red-brown branching roots. Poppy capsule with flower, cornflower, chicory, scabious or teasel.

Two plants. Main: stem with broad fan-shaped toothed leaves; a huge top flower head: a red-brown conical/funnel receptacle striped with pale flame marks, crowned by a wide ring of white petals each tipped with dark blue/green beads around a pale dotted disc; root a cluster of round brown and red bulbs/tubers. Small left plant: three fan leaves with a cluster of round brown bulbs. Thistle/artichoke-like head over bulbs: saffron/crocus or onion bulbs, cyclamen, or turnip/radish.

Tall single stem with paired, cup- or fan-shaped pale green leaves (or bracts) whose upper edges are fringed with small curled tendril/bead tips, arranged like a ladder; a pale scaly cone/bud at the top; brown root forking into two with fibrous rootlets. Fumitory, yarrow, mugwort, tansy or a fringed-bract plant (lady's mantle, saxifrage).

Plant with deeply cut, curly-edged, crisped leaves (parsley/celery/carrot-like) on long stalks spreading from a pale crown; a broad fan of fine stalks topped with a dense umbel/head of many tiny dark blue dots or florets; two long red spindle roots (carrot/radish-like) crossing each other. Umbellifer with tap roots: carrot, parsnip, parsley, or mandrake-like crossed roots; also scabious.

Long thin stem with one large broad ovate leaf at the top, green with pale veins (variegated); halfway down a small red three-lobed (trefoil-like) leaf cluster; long horizontal root with forked rootlets. Variegated broad leaf suggests plantain, arum or lungwort; red trefoil suggests wood sorrel or herb Robert.

Single straight stem with a basal rosette of five broad elliptic smooth green leaves; at the top a small pale yellow star-shaped flower (or star of bracts) with a dark eye-like centre (a red/black 'eye' with brows); simple red forked roots. A decorative flourish/ligature sits above the first paragraph. Star-of-Bethlehem, plantain, gentian, or a lily with a star flower.

A colony: about nine stems standing on a long horizontal root mass with many hanging red roots; their leafy crowns of small green comma-shaped leaves merge into one continuous hedge/canopy; each stem topped by a small cup-shaped flower head with a yellow and white rim (like a small daisy or marigold head). Ground-cover colony: chamomile, yarrow, tansy, cotton thistle or a reed/rush bed.

Two plants. Left: thin stem with narrow lanceolate leaves in clusters and a small white flower at the top, growing from a coiled, snake-like hairy brown root (S-shaped like a serpent). Right: bushy plant with curled, hook/crescent-shaped dark green leaves on long stalks and many small spiky/bristly blue-and-white bead clusters at the stalk tips, from a pale fibrous root. The snake-shaped root suggests bistort / snakeroot / dragonwort.

Tall red-striped stem rising from a long horizontal spiny/thorny red root (like a centipede or a thorny branch); a dense umbrella/fountain of long drooping leaves striped green and dark blue; at the top a small cup flower with pale yellow and white petals over green sepals. Leek/onion fan, iris, yucca-like leaves, or a spiny-rooted plant (restharrow, eryngo).

A tuft of oblong, crisped/lobed green leaves (like lettuce, endive or oak-leaf) on short stalks from a knobbly crown ringed with round stubs; two pale pink-red ribbed, striped vase-shaped buds/capsules with fringed tops on a thin red stalk; pale trunk-like root with two spreading arms. Lettuce or endive with flower buds, poppy capsules, or a dandelion/chicory rosette.

Three stems from a thick pink-brown branching root (with ring joints and a horn-shaped tip); each stem with alternate triangular leaves (some green, some tan/brown and drooping like dried) and on top a curving branched spike of small blue pinnate/comb-like leaflets or flower sprays. Fern, mugwort/wormwood, horsetail, or a goosefoot (Chenopodium) with triangular leaves.

Three upright stems with paired, scalloped-edged, half-green half-white leaflets (a few olive/yellow), each topped by a cluster of small dark blue berries or buds; a long horizontal creeping root with round red-and-white nodes (like a chain of eyes) branching from a white knobbed crown. Self-heal/bugle, bilberry, a creeping rhizome herb, or grape hyacinth.

Three stems side by side on a single long horizontal olive rhizome with many hanging roots; each with a column of large curved, wing-like green leaves on one side (like flags or feathers) and a small daisy/composite flower head with yellow centre and white petals at the top. A rhizomatous colony with composite flowers: coltsfoot, butterbur, elecampane, arnica, tansy, or chamomile.

Two large lanceolate leaves with strongly serrated/toothed edges (nettle/betony/thistle-like) from a short stem; above, a branched candelabra of stalks carrying about nine nodding composite flower heads with blue-edged bracts, white fringed petals and yellow/orange dotted discs; fibrous brown root with two small red horn-like marks at the crown. Composite with toothed leaves: elecampane, tansy, ox-eye, feverfew, sneezewort, arnica or sow-thistle.

Two broad lobed, scalloped leaf masses (like a cabbage or a large kidney leaf with rounded lobes) joined by a long thin curving stalk: a smaller leaf at upper right, a very large one at the bottom; small red bulb/root at the base with fine rootlets. Coltsfoot/butterbur, marsh mallow, ground ivy, asarabacca, or lady's mantle.

Thick stem with broad, smooth elliptical leaves (plantain/tobacco-like) in two tiers; three long slender stalks each topped by a blue five-petalled star flower with a brown centre (like borage or forget-me-not); brown root with long spreading arms and small pink tips at the crown. Borage, plantain, gentian, periwinkle or flax.

Stem with alternate, cup-shaped green leaves each ending in long curling finger/tentacle-like tips (like a hand or an octopus); three round, pale, seed-dotted heads on stalks at the top (like opened seed cups or dandelion/poppy heads); fine fibrous root. Fumitory, crowfoot/buttercup (finger leaves), lady's mantle, sundew-like, or a poppy.

Two branching stems with many small, deeply crisped/frilled dark green leaves (parsley/curled-mint/oak-leaf-like); at the top of each stem a pair of round flower heads or fruits, blue-black with yellow caps, set in a green star-shaped calyx; fine fibrous root. Curled parsley, wormwood/mugwort, tansy, columbine, or a nightshade-type berry in a calyx.

A long, wavy pale stem winding up from a pale olive root drawn as looping bulbous shapes (one end like an animal or snake head); two large round dark green leaf masses (cloud-like, scalloped); many small red tubular/bell flowers with frilled mouths hanging along the winding stems, and at the top dark blue fringed flowers on red calyces. Climber with red tubular flowers: honeysuckle/woodbine, bindweed, fuchsia-like; snake-head root suggests snakeroot or bryony.

A single tall thin stem from a round knobby, bubble-textured bulb or tuber (like a cluster of eyes); at the top a round crown made of five large curled, crescent/claw-shaped leaves in green and olive with small blue inner marks, round a pale centre; a small blue five-petalled flower at the upper right corner. Notable: a column of single symbols down the left margin beside the first paragraph, the first five resembling the numerals 1-5 (possibly a later hand), suggesting a numbered list or alphabet key.

Stem with fan-shaped leaves with crinkled/toothed (frilly) edges, each marked with a large dark blue teardrop blotch; a huge round flower head on top: a fringed ring of blue and white petals and hairy filaments round an oval pale 'eye' with a small drawn mark (letter-like) at its centre; spreading brown roots. Spotted leaves again suggest lungwort, spotted orchid or persicaria; eye-like flower might pun on eyebright or ox-eye.

Short stem with a pair of broad, layered, rounded pale green leaves (like folded cabbage or bulb leaves); three long stalks from the top bearing one large nodding blue flower head made of many curled, hooked, tentacle-like blue petals around a pale dotted dome, with a green round bud in the middle; pale-orange root with wavy-edged spreading arms. Columbine, aconite, love-in-a-mist, sea holly, or pasque flower.

Straight stem from a red-brown root that twists into two crossing legs (like human legs or a forked mandrake); four leaves drawn like beetles or bugs: oval green bodies with a pale dotted midline and curled leg-like projections; at the top five round red-and-white rosette flowers (five petals, round centre) on long stalks from bulb-like pale calyces. Legged root suggests mandrake; bug-shaped leaves might pun on a name (scorpion, beetle, 'cimex', louse-wort).

Tall stem with long, strap-like green leaves that curl and loop around the stem like ribbons or snakes; top a tall spike of many small hanging blue berries/bells on short curved stalks, with two long arching side sprays of the same; pale root with broad flat lobes. Grape hyacinth, bluebell, solomon's seal, or a climber with dark berries (bryony, bittersweet); looping leaves might suggest a twining vine or a snake pun.

Two plants. Main: stem with clusters of long narrow pointed leaves with comb-toothed tips; top a small cluster flower with blue petals in a green cup; root a bulbous red-brown ring shape with eye-like knobs (like a face or a heart) on a horizontal bar with knobbed ends. Small left plant: narrow toothed leaves on a short stem joined to the same bar. Bulb plus face-like root: onion, garlic, cyclamen, mandrake, or a lily bulb.

Single stem with alternate leaves drawn as round, curled, spiky balls (each like a curled hedgehog or a crumpled spiny leaf with a hole), from a pale forked root with a split crown. Spiny curled leaves: holly, thistle, butcher's broom, prickly lettuce, or a 'hedgehog' name pun.

Winding pale stem with alternate oval spiny-edged leaves coloured green, olive, brown and orange-brown (bristly like cocklebur leaves or burr fruits); top branches carry many small daisy-like flowers with red-streaked bases and a single large drooping flower head with a ring of white petals round a dotted oval disc and a red-streaked cup; root drawn as a strange geometric olive-brown block/chain shape (like a key or broken loop). Burr-bearing plant: cocklebur, burdock, thistle, or a chamomile-type composite.

Pale stem with opposite pairs of long lanceolate, finely serrated leaves crossing each other at right angles; at the top two/three daisy-like flowers with red-tipped petals round white dotted centres, over blue-black pointed bracts; brown cylindrical root collar with fine fibrous roots. Willow-herb, loosestrife, pink, hemp-agrimony, or a red-rayed composite (marigold, ox-eye).

Branching stem with pinnate leaves of narrow, bristly-edged leaflets (like fern, vetch or tansy); two stems at the top each ending in a long scaly green cone (pine-cone or hop-cone texture) crowned by a tuft of small red-and-white flowers; stem base with pale feathery sheaths; roots drawn as long feather-like serrated strands. Hop (cone), pineapple-like spike, mugwort, tansy, teasel, or a feathery-rooted fern.

Red stem with alternate long-pointed lanceolate leaves on reddish petioles; a long arching raceme curving over to the right, hung with many dark blue oval pods/berries with pale dotted tips (like seed capsules or closed bells); root a chain of rounded red-brown tubers (like beads or a string of potatoes). Tuber chain suggests dropwort, tuberous comfrey, or an orchid/asphodel; the hanging blue capsules suggest bluebell, Solomon's seal or a nightshade.

Three stems from a bulbous cup-like crown with tangled roots; each with alternate fan-shaped leaves with fringed/toothed edges; each stem ends in a large red elongated sac/pod (like a chili or an elongated bud) from whose tip a small round blue-and-white flower emerges. Red pod plus flower: winter cherry (red inflated calyx), pomegranate flower, red bladder campion, or fuchsia-like.

A single huge lanceolate/tulip-shaped leaf sheath (several overlapping pointed leaves like a closed bud or a leek) pierced by a tall red-brown stem; at the top a red fan of stalks carrying a dense head of small blue and green cubes/squares (like a pixelated umbel or a cluster of tiny bells); red-brown branching root ending in an octopus/animal-like shape with a head at right. Leek/onion (umbel on a stalk, sheathing leaves), garlic, squill, or saffron.

Stem from a braided/plaited pale root; two lower branches each ending in a dark blue rounded mass surrounded by a fan of long green needle-like rays (like a thistle head or sea urchin); a blue convolvulus-like open trumpet flower at the top and a blue folded bud on the left; on the right a curling spiral (crozier) stem bearing long dark blue pointed leaflets radiating like rays (like a fern fiddlehead or a sunburst). Fern crozier, scorpion's-tail, thistle, or bindweed.

A single stem from a forked red root bearing two large palm-like fans of long narrow toothed leaflets (like a palm frond, fern or hemp leaf); at the upper right a small pale curled fan/plume shape (like a feather, crest or rolled frond) with a dark blue caterpillar- or burr-like bristly body hanging from it. Palm, fern, date palm, or reed; the bristly blue object could be a fruit cluster or a caterpillar/insect pun.

Tall branching shrub-like plant with many deeply lobed, star/palmate, crinkled leaves (geranium/crane's-bill/mallow-like); several blue bell- or trumpet-shaped flowers (dark blue at top, paler blue on lower branches); thick hairy/fibrous brown root mass with two spreading lobes. Crane's-bill (meadow crane's-bill: blue flowers, palmate leaves), monkshood, larkspur, bellflower or mallow.

Non-plant page: a circular diagram of four concentric rings. The outer and third rings carry continuous text. The second ring holds a run of about 17 isolated single glyphs that repeats four times around the circle (each run starting with the same ornate symbol), like an alphabet, a key, a sequence of numerals, or a calendar of signs. In the centre, four human half-figures (one curly-haired, one long-haired, one with a hand raised, one reclining) reach toward a central rosette/cloud with a dot, each with a short label. A small 'S'-like mark in the lower right corner. Four figures plus a fourfold repeat suggest the four winds, seasons, elements, humours, ages of man, or quarters of the world/heavens.

Non-plant page: full page of continuous text in three long paragraphs, with no drawing except three small eight-rayed stars in the left margin marking the start of each paragraph (one at the top, two further down). Possibly a prose section with star-marked items, a table of contents, an astronomical or medical text, or recipes.

Non-plant page: full page of continuous text in four paragraphs, no drawing; a single small eight-rayed star at the top-left margin by the first line. Like 58r, a star-marked prose page (perhaps the end of a section or a long recipe/commentary text).

Plant with many deeply cut, toothed oak-leaf/celery-like leaves on long stalks from one crown; at the top a branched umbrella of pale star-shaped flowers (6-pointed, dotted centres, uncoloured), like an umbel; root a red-brown bulb sending out chains of spindle/teardrop-shaped tubers on runners. Three short words of script are written beside the plant (a label). Umbellifer with tubers: earth-nut/pignut, water dropwort, parsley, celery, or meadowsweet/dropwort.

Tall branching green stems (several looping into hook/crozier curls) from a brown fibrous root; many small round dark green fruiting heads with fringed pale edges at the branch tips (like burrs, scabious or sea-holly heads); a single blue tufted flower with a cup-shaped green calyx at the top. A short text in two columns at the lower middle. Scabious, teasel, burdock, devil's-bit or globe thistle.

Non-plant page: full page of text in paragraphs. Down the left margin runs a column of single glyphs, one at the start of each line, and to its left a separate column of short words (like a key, index, line labels or a list of items). At the bottom left a small sketch of a naked human figure lying on the ground (as if dead, asleep or sick), near a small tub/barrel or cup and two round objects (loaves, pills, coins); a few faint Latin-script letters beside them read roughly 'v / den mus / del' (later hand?), and a line of the manuscript's own script above. Reclining figure might mean a patient, death, a bath, or the 'sick-bed' (aegrotus).

Short stem with three large fan/shell-shaped leaf masses drawn as stacked green arched bands (like ribbed scallop shells or folded cabbage leaves): a big one at top, two at the sides; two small flowers in the middle (pale yellow-white cups with blue centres); red-brown root with three pointed arms. Text block above. Faint pencil/ink sketch of a small figure near the bottom left. Cabbage, savoy, lettuce, a ribbed-leaf plantain, or hart's-tongue fern.

Fold-out with two astronomical diagrams. Left panel (67r1): a pale human face in a crescent moon at the centre, surrounded by about 16-17 pointed rays alternately red, blue and star-filled pale; an outer ring divided into matching sectors, each with one or two gold eight-pointed stars and a short label; two rings of continuous text outside; a text block above. Right panel (67r2): a wheel of 12 sectors, each with a small face in a moon/planet disc (several half-red, like phases) and text; a central eight-pointed star; an outer band of red labels separated by tally-mark ticks; three lines of text (one red) below. 12 sectors suggest months, zodiac signs or hours; moon faces suggest lunar phases or a lunar calendar; the ray wheel suggests lunar mansions or the moon's course through the signs.

Fold-out with two diagrams. Left panel (67v2): a central square (green corners, swirling multicoloured disc inside) with eight arms. Four cardinal arms end in small cloud/flame shapes. Four diagonal arms end in hand- or cloud-like shapes with blue, one of them a rayed sun face half behind a blue cloud. Each corner has a small group of three or four faces joined by lines (like stick constellations or molecules). At bottom left, a disc quartered green, blue, red and pale, holding four faces joined by lines. Right panel (67v1): a central sun face with a blue headband and wavy rays; about 12 radial lines of text run outwards between many gold (some green) stars; the outer ring is broken into labelled segments separated by small crenellated, tower- or box-like marks with dots. The left reads like a world/weather diagram (four quarters, winds, clouds, the elements); the right like a sun-and-stars or twelve-houses diagram.

Three-panel fold-out of star charts. Panel 1 (68r1): a field of about 28 gold eight-pointed stars, each with a one-word label (a star catalogue), a sun-like face disc at the top and a crescent moon face at the bottom, with a text block above. Panel 2 (68r2): a dense field of about 60 stars, about 20 of them labelled, a crescent moon face at the top and a disc at the bottom with a face ringed in blue and white, with text above. Panel 3 (68r3): a circle with a central face (sun or moon) and eight radial sectors full of stars arranged in rows. At upper left is a tight cluster of six or seven tiny stars on a stalk, labelled (very like the Pleiades). Text runs round the rim and along the radii. Star names, constellations, Pleiades/Seven Sisters, sun and moon.

Three-panel fold-out. Panel 3 (68v3, left): a spiral/vortex diagram. A central disc holds short labels. Around it is a broad ring speckled blue (like water, cloud or sky) with gold stars and a scalloped/frilled edge, from which four or five curved arms of text sweep out like a pinwheel to an outer text circle; text block above. It looks like a whirlpool, the turning heavens, wind, or a coiled cloud. Panel 2 (68v2, middle): a central eight-petalled blue flower/star with a gold centre, with radial lines of text dividing a field of gold stars into sectors. Panel 1 (68v1, right): a central face (moon or sun) with about 16 long blue and pale star-filled rays, surrounded by stars and radial text. Celestial vortex/whirl, rotation of the heavens, the sky, Milky Way, or seasons/winds.

Circular diagram: a central gold five- or six-pointed star (with tiny single glyphs between its points) inside a small text ring; about 28 radial spokes alternately coloured green, blue and plain, each sector carrying a short line of text; an outer ring of 28 small petal/bead shapes (coloured green and blue), forming a scalloped rim; an outer text band divided into segments; a text block above. Twenty-eight divisions strongly suggests the 28 lunar mansions (days of the moon's month); otherwise a wheel of days, a compass/wind rose or a calendar wheel.

Three-panel fold-out. Panel 1 (69v): a wheel with a pale centre (a faint star or flower) from which about 24-28 thick spokes radiate, coloured green and blue and drawn like tubes, with text between them and text rings outside. Panel 2 (70r1): a central disc with six or seven thin spokes, inside a thick pale ring and a broad scalloped band speckled blue (like water, clouds or a wreath), with text rings outside. Panel 3 (70r2): a central sun or moon face inside an eight-pointed star of blue-shaded, triangular rays, ringed by text, with a column of continuous text to its right. Spokes again suggest lunar days/mansions; the speckled band suggests water, clouds, the sea or the ocean round the world; the rayed face suggests the sun or moon among the planets.

Zodiac page: Pisces. In the centre, two fish lying head to tail on a wavy blue water line, with the Latin-script month label 'mars' (March) written between them in a different hand; two stars nearby. Round them, in two concentric rings, about 30 small half-length human figures, mostly women, many nude. Most stand in or rise from small striped or patterned tubs/barrels; each holds or is tied to a gold star with a short label. A ring band of tally-like vertical strokes runs between the rings. Text circles the whole. A sign with 30 figures fits the 30 degrees or days of Pisces; the figures might be souls, stars, or day/degree personifications.
candidates_en: thirty days / degrees of the sign

pages.description: Zodiac page: Aries. In the centre a dark/olive horned goat or ram with curved horns, nibbling a green bush or tree on a water line; Latin-script month label 'abril' (April) beside it. Two concentric rings of about 15 small figures each, mostly clothed women, some in patterned barrels/tubs, each holding a gold star on a string; labels next to each; text circling. The first of the two Aries pages (light/dark Aries pair).
candidates_en: thirty days / degrees of the sign

pages.description: Zodiac page: Aries (second, coloured version). Centre: a pale horned ram/goat eating from a green plant on a green wavy ground, with the Latin-script month label 'abril' (April). Two rings of clothed women and men in coloured dress (red, blue, green), several standing in patterned tubs or barrels, each holding a gold star; about 10 inner and 15 outer figures (about 25 here, perhaps 30 together with the companion Aries page). Labels beside each, with text round the rings.

Four-panel fold-out of zodiac wheels (scan at low resolution). 71v: Taurus, a pale red-brown bull standing on green ground, with clothed figures in coloured dress in tubs holding stars. 72r1: Taurus again, a solid red bull on green ground, with a small label below. 72r2: Gemini, a man in green and a woman in blue facing each other and holding hands, with a label between them. 72r3: Cancer, a small red crayfish or crab at the centre. All four have two rings of mostly nude figures holding stars and text rings. The central labels are in Latin script but too small to read at this resolution. By position they are likely the months of the Aries-to-Cancer sequence: Taurus 'may', Gemini 'jun' and Cancer 'jul' are expected.

Two-panel fold-out of zodiac wheels. 72v3 (left): Leo, a pale lion or dog-like beast with blue marks before a small tree, with the Latin-script label 'augst' (August), possibly read 'aougst'. 72v2 (right): Virgo, a woman in a blue dress with a blue hat, holding a star in one hand and a small flower at her feet, with a short Latin-script label to her left (perhaps 'septembre'; hard to read). Both have rings of nude female figures, many with stars, and text circling.

Zodiac page: Libra. Centre: a pair of balance scales hanging from a beam on a post, with blue-filled pans and the Latin-script label 'octebre' or 'octembre' (October). Two rings of nude women, some crowned, many holding stars, with labels and text circling. A hole in the vellum at right.

Zodiac page: Scorpio. Centre: a small green-grey four-legged beast with a long curled tail (lizard, salamander or dragon-like rather than a true scorpion) under a gold star, with the Latin-script label 'novebre' (November). Rings of nude women, some crowned, each holding a gold star, about 30 in all, with labels; four extra figures stand outside the top of the circle.

Zodiac page: Sagittarius. Centre: a man in a blue tunic and a pale broad hat walking and holding a crossbow (not a centaur archer), with a small scrawled Latin-script label at his feet (perhaps 'decembre', December). Rings of nude women holding stars, with labels and text rings. The last zodiac page in this run; Capricorn and Aquarius are not present here.

Bathing/'biological' section: a long green-filled channel or tube runs down from a domed, ribbed canopy at the top (like a fountain head, an umbrella or the sky with rays and beads) into a large green pool. Small nude women stand or lie in the stream and the pool, one in a small round tub. A second green pool at lower right holds a group of about six nude women dancing or bathing, with a large faint woman (crowned?) outside. Labels and dense text all around. Bathing in green (mineral?) water, springs, baths, fertility or anatomy (vessels and organs) are all possible readings.

Bathing section: at the top a long scaly, ringed tube (like a pipe, a snake or a gut) with a blue knob comes down into a long horizontal basin filled with blue rays (water or light). A row of ten pipes or tubes, each labelled, hangs from it, and below them ten nude women sit in a green tub/pool, each under her own pipe as if receiving water (a shower bath). At the bottom a blue-green basin is packed with about 20 nude women, with a long thin tube or stream running out of it downward. Dense text throughout. Showers, baths, springs, water pipes, intestines or the circulation of fluids.

Non-plant page in the bathing section: a full page of text in paragraphs with no drawing, and single glyphs in the left margin beside some lines (a few letter-like marks, like a key or numbering). Probably commentary or instructions for the surrounding bath/fluid illustrations, or recipes.

Bathing section: text paragraphs with small drawings in the margins. Top right: a nude figure standing in a tub, holding up a bowl/cup from which drops or particles spray. Left margin from top: a tall layered cone/fir-shaped object (like a bush, a beehive or a flame) with a nude woman beside it holding a sprig; a nude woman standing on a pipe/pedestal holding a red-and-blue striped bag, pouch or fruit (like an organ, a bladder or a purse); a woman seated on a scaly, coiled cone-like structure (like a shell or a wave), and below her another woman tangled in a scaled tube that ends in a dotted spray. Labels throughout. Bags/pouches suggest bladders, wombs or purses; sprays suggest springs or showers.

Bathing section: across the top a long green-banded tube or arch with five openings on its underside, each emitting a drop or spray (one red-orange flame-like); at each end a nude woman in a tub, the left one releasing liquid streams down the margin, the right one in a tub with a spray. Lower left: a woman sitting in a tub on a large coiled, octopus-like tube system with spouts and a blue knob emitting spray, linked by a tube to another woman holding a blue ball beside a blue scaly/ridged object (like a shell, lung or wing). Labels throughout. Looks like plumbing, distillation, or anatomy (vessels, lungs, intestines).

Bathing section: at the top three nude women connected by curved tubes and pipes: the left in a striped round basin, the middle one standing in a blue pool with three droplet shapes hanging below, the right one lying on a large blue-and-white scaled (wave/feather) mound. In the margins: a woman in a striped tub holding a tube that empties down; a woman beside a long coiled tube that zigzags and pours a stream; a crowned woman standing in a cup on a pedestal (like a chalice or font) holding a horn-like object; a woman in a green-filled basin under a blue falling spray at lower right. Labels by each. Fountains, conduits, baptismal font, horns of plenty; perhaps anatomy (kidneys, bladders, urine).

Bathing section: at the top two fan-shaped, ribbed, scaled objects (like shells, fans, gills, or the ends of a funnel) joined by a horizontal pipe made of linked barrel/cylinder segments with red insides, which turns down into a vertical chain of cups; from its tip a blue stream falls into a large round green pool holding about eight nude women, many lying or embracing. A blue stream runs from this pool down to a second green pool holding about ten women, with a small drop-like object below. Text wraps round. Linked segments suggest pipes, a distilling train, an intestine, or vertebrae.

Bathing section: a long green pool or bath in which about nine nude women sit side by side, set on a long building-like base with an arcade of small blue round-arched windows or arches (like a bath house, aqueduct or furnace stoke-holes). A thin blue stream curls down the left margin into it from the top. Text above and below. A heated public bath (stufa) with a hypocaust/arched furnace, or an aqueduct-fed bath.

Bathing section: down the left margin a vertical chain of figures linked by pipes and streams. Top: a nude figure under a blue, beaded, coiled tube. Then a twisted blue spiral or shell object pouring into a pipe, a woman standing on a blue basin, two women standing in cups joined by a stream, two more in a blue-water basin, and finally a stream pouring into a large green pool at the bottom where a woman sits holding a curved object. A large faint green-blue stain or wash runs across the bottom of the page. The rest is dense text in paragraphs. A cascade of baths, a fountain with basins, or a distillation series.

Bathing section. Down the left margin is a chain of scenes. A blue umbrella-like fountain canopy sprays onto a woman in a tub who holds up a small cross or flower. A woman lies along a pipe. A woman holds a blue bowl at a blue pool. Pipes lead down to a long green pool at the bottom, where a woman sits beside a large spotted, many-toed lizard- or salamander-like creature (blue-spotted). Small animals are drawn round the pool: a dog- or fox-like quadruped at bottom left, a pale weasel/ferret, a cat-like animal, and a bird-like or red creature at the right edge. The animals may name medicines or springs.

Bathing section. Across the top is a frieze of about nine nude women. One is crowned and sits in a blue tub, one wears clothes (a red robe), and several make gestures. A pipe down the right side pours into a long blue river or pool under the middle text block. A crowned woman bathes in it at the right; two women stand at the left, one holding a small object. Lower down: a crowned woman in a cup-shaped vessel holding out a ring or flower, and at right a woman in a footed goblet/chalice with roots or tassels hanging below.

Bathing section. Top left: a crowned woman sits on a frilly, scalloped round basin with blue drips, holding out a long pipe or horn. Top right: a woman in a blue-and-white scalloped basin. Left margin: a woman's face peering from a large hairy or fuzzy oval object (like a fleece, a cloud or a hedgehog), then women standing in cups or funnels on stems with dripping spouts. Right margin: women in tubs, and a woman whose lower body is a long scaly green tail (a mermaid or serpent-woman). A long blue river with three or four women runs across the bottom.

Bathing section. Two long green pools, each holding a row of seven or six nude women, are joined by a long thin blue pipe that runs down the left side. The lower pool is set in a wooden tub with vertical staves, like a barrel or cask. Text sits between them.

Bathing section. A large green pool or tub holds two rows of about eight nude women each, about 16 in all. A wavy green stream runs into its upper left corner from a long stalk-like channel in the margin. A label sits beside the tub at left, and a cord or tassel hangs from its right corner. Text above.

Bathing section. At the top is an arched pipe with a red-and-blue segmented column or spindle in the middle (like a valve, distilling column or stack of vessels); a woman at left stands on a stacked, turned pedestal holding the pipe, and a woman at right sits in a blue basin. In the middle a horizontal pipe has a woman at its left end in a blue tub on a heart-shaped cup and a feathery brush/broom shape midway. Beside it is a star or wheel-shaped valve, and a blue star with a small ring at right. A woman reclines in a green-lined trough on a funnel stand. At the bottom a big green, lumpy pool or mound holds about ten women (several crowned, one with a sprig, one emerging from a stream), with spray fountains rising from it and labels around it.

Bathing section. Top: a woman on a goblet-shaped stand holds a blue-and-red looped tube; a woman with long hair, wearing a green garment, sits on a blue cloud or rock, beside a large rainbow of several coloured arcs (red, yellow, blue) with a scaly or dotted fan (rain or cloud) above it; a woman at top right stands in a funnel cup. Left margin: a woman inside a green horseshoe- or arch-shaped tube on a stand. Right: a woman in a tub with blue-dotted drops below. Bottom: a large green pool or hill crossed by two blue rainbow-like arcs; a woman stands in a cup holding a green pipe; a feathered or spiny stalk; women in tubs at the left.

Bathing section. Left margin, top to bottom: a woman pours from a spouted jug or watering can, spraying drops; a woman sits on a striped, coiled cone or shell; another sits in a woven, scaly basket on a cone dripping water. Lower left: a large blue arched pipe or rainbow-shaped tube connects a woman whose lower half is a blue scaly fish-tail (a mermaid) with a red girdle at left, and a woman standing in a pale tube at right; this tube descends to a blue, many-legged, star- or octopus-like object (like a sea anemone, a spider, a kidney or a root ball) with dotted spray. Labels throughout.

Bathing section. Centre: two large round green bulbous vessels or sacs (like gourds, flasks, lungs or ovaries) joined at their necks by braided, rope-like knotted tubes that spill a dotted stream. A woman at left holds one vessel's spout while standing in a scaly cone-shaped tube; a woman at right stands in a fringed tube under a green arm. Top left: a woman in a woven basket holding a long tube that ends in a fork with drops. Lower right: a woman wrapped in a pale and blue cloak or shell sits on a green Y- or X-shaped forked tube with open ends. Twin round vessels suggest kidneys, lungs, ovaries/testicles, gourds or distilling flasks.

Bathing section. Top: a long green pool of about 15 nude women under a canopy of blue-and-white scale- or net-like arches with pendant blue drops and tassels (like a roofed bath house, a cloud ceiling or rain). A blue stream runs down the left margin to a second green pool of about ten women, one holding a blue bowl and one a red cup, and on to a third, blue-and-white swirling pool of about 12 women at the bottom left. Labels between the arches.

Bathing section. Two oval pools of blue swirling water, each crowded with nude women (about eight to ten each), connected by a long wavy blue stream that comes from a scaly, fringed fan or showerhead at top right and continues down past the bottom of the page. Labels at right.
Non-plant page: a full page of text in about nine short paragraphs with no drawing. Part of the large 85-86 fold-out sheet. Probably prose (recipes, instructions or a commentary).

Cosmological fold-out panels. Left panel: a central blue whirlpool disc with a sun face, ringed by four small figures (people or heads in clouds, one clothed in blue) at the cardinal points. From it, four long arms run diagonally to fan-, shell- or trumpet-shaped clouds at the corners (like wind-blowers). Text fills the quadrants between the arms and runs round the rim. A small figure or sign sits at the top. Middle panel: a pale disc with a small crescent moon face at the centre, inside many concentric rings of scale- or cell-like bubbles, some coloured blue, with text rings outside and text below. Right panel: a full page of continuous text. The left panel reads like a diagram of the four winds and the world (sun in the middle, winds at the corners); the middle one like the moon inside the heavenly spheres, clouds or elements.

Two panels from the 85-86 fold-out. Left: a full page of continuous text in paragraphs. Right: four large scaled, segmented funnel- or trumpet-shaped objects at the corners (like spouts, tubes, horns or cornucopias, with rows of blue-dotted scales and fringed rims). The two upper ones pour dotted sprays into the middle. One lower one has a small figure or creature on top and a toothed comb-like spray. Short text blocks sit in the centre and along the sides, some upside down. Faint pencil sketches lie in the middle. The arrangement matches the four-corner winds of the panel above (wind-blowers or rain-spouts), or else four springs or rivers.

Large nine-part fold-out ('rosettes'): nine circular or oval medallions in a 3x3 grid, joined by broad bands of scale- and bubble-like texture, wavy tubes and causeways. Text labels are scattered throughout. Top left: an oval of blue and white bead rings with long tube-like spouts attached. Top middle: a star of blue and gold rays inside a ring of white oval cells (like a rose window or a flower). Top right: a big disc of many small stars inside a scalloped cloud border. Attached to its left side is a small drawing of a crenellated castle or walled tower with a battlemented gate, and a fan of feathers or rays sits at its upper right. Centre: a large oval of bubble rings, inside which stand several tall columns or pillars topped with turned capitals, holding a blue dotted canopy (like a temple, a fountain hall or a bath house). Middle left and middle right: pale rosettes of radiating lobes. Bottom left: a cloud-bordered disc with a central blue-dotted oval, wavy blue shapes and two dumbbell shapes. Off to the left is a small circle containing a T- or Y-shaped figure, like a compass, clock face or T-O world map. Bottom middle: a blue and gold eight-rayed star. Bottom right: a disc with stars, a block of parallel bars (like stairs, a bridge or a grille) and a blue X-shaped cross. A small rayed sun face sits in the extreme top-left and bottom-right corners. Interpretations include a map of the world or of a region (towns, castles, rivers, roads), the heavens and paradise, a bath complex fed by springs, or the organs of the body.

Plant page, in a later section of the manuscript. A single stem has two rosettes of broad spoon-shaped, smooth green leaves, one above the other. At the top, three nodding flower clusters of narrow blue-and-white tubular florets hang from scaly green receptacles (like cornflower or scabious heads, or a clustered bell flower). The root is a thick red-brown knotted crown with long tentacle-like arms, almost like a figure or an octopus. A faint orange X-shaped mark and green offset stains lie on the left.

Two plants. Left: a rosette of broad spoon-shaped leaves with a single small white daisy-like flower on a stalk, over a thick red-brown forked root. Right: a fern-like plant with pinnate, finely toothed fronds and two tall stalks topped by umbels of about 20 pale cup-shaped capsules, each with a red rim (seed capsules or flowers), over a thick red-brown, many-armed root. Text is wrapped round both, and a marginal line of text runs vertically at the left. The right plant suggests an umbellifer (hemlock, cow parsley, carrot, fennel) or yarrow; the left suggests a daisy or chamomile.

Pharmaceutical section. Down the left margin stand three tall ornate apothecary jars or vessels (albarelli or turned containers), banded red, green and white, with lids, footed bases and flared stands. To the right are rows of small drawings of separate plant parts, each with a one-word label: pieces of roots (some cut, scaly, forked, one like a pine cone or corm), leaves, a sprig of pointed leaves, a spiny/fringed seed head or burr, a carrot-shaped root, and a big pale branching root at lower right. A long pale bulbous root lies along the bottom. Each labelled part probably names a medicinal simple: a root, leaf or seed kept in the jars. Strong candidate for an ingredient list or recipe with the jars as containers.

Three-panel pharmaceutical fold-out (88v, 89r1, 89r2). Each panel has a column of ornate jars or vessels down the margin. 88v has tall red-and-white stacked albarello-like jars. 89r1 has slimmer jars, including one with a red bulb and a red dotted globe-shaped flask. 89r2 has green-and-red banded jars and goblets. Between the text paragraphs are many small labelled plant parts: roots (forked, bulbous, carrot-like, tangled), leaves (single, star-shaped, spiny, ivy-like), a spiny caterpillar-like fruit or pod (like a cucumber or a teasel head), bulbs, and a large green leafy plant. Each part carries a short label. Several parts are coloured green (leaves) or orange/brown (roots).

Pharmaceutical section, part of the 89v fold-out. Down the left margin are three ornate vessels: a green and blue domed jar with a finial on a footed stand; a tall blue-and-white tiered flask; and a round blue bottle on a stand. To the right are labelled drawings of plant parts: tangled tan roots, a red-brown looped or knotted root, a green ladle- or pear-shaped leaf, a spreading pale branching root, a large round green fringed leaf mass (like a lettuce or cabbage) above a red-brown fleshy root with many tentacles (something like a hand, a beet or a radish), and several round, lobed green leaves (like lady's mantle or mallow) with tangled roots at the bottom.

Three panels. Left (89v part 2), pharmaceutical: two ornate jars in the margin, a green goblet with a scaly lid and a tall blue-banded flask, plus labelled roots and leaves: a tan root with fringe, a white root with sprigs, an oak-like lobed leaf, a green leaf like a bird or fish, a red-brown fist-shaped root, small green leaves with roots, and a big spreading tan root at the bottom. Middle (90r1), plant: a stem with four spiky green tufts (like teasels or thistle heads) on a knobbed base with a face-like knot; two long stalks curve up to two large round dark blue fruits or flowers, each with a ribbed pale cup (like poppy capsules, blueberries or globe flowers); spreading fibrous roots. Right (90r2), plant: a tree-like plant with many round teal-green leaves or berries on branching stems and a row of six cup- or trumpet-shaped seed pods along the top; a round white bulb, then a horizontal brown rhizome with round knots.

Bushy plant with many slender branches set with paired, narrow, willow-like pointed leaves (pale and darker green, finely veined). At the top are three white thistle-like or brush-like flower heads, each sitting in a green star-shaped cup. The root is a thick red-brown crown splitting into many long roots. Green offset stains lie on the left. Like a centaury, knapweed, safflower, a willow-leaved composite, or rosemary-leaved thistle.

Plant with a central stem and spreading branches of large, pointed, triangular teal leaves (like arrowheads or a fern) in pairs. Three tall stalks end in four-armed star or cross-shaped flowers, white with dark blue claws or stamens and blue centres (like a periwinkle, a passion flower, or a cross-shaped crucifer flower). The root is drawn as an animal: a long tan body with two clawed feet, like a lizard, a dog or a mandrake-beast walking along the bottom.

A single stem with about 16 broad crescent- or sickle-shaped teal leaves in opposite pairs, ladder-like, along a red-veined stem. At the top is a large olive-tan conical or dome-shaped head (like a sunflower disc seen from the side, or a hat or mushroom cap) covered in rows of small dark dots (seeds), with a fringed rim. Many fine red roots. The seed-packed dome suggests a sunflower-type head, a giant composite, an artichoke, or a castor or plantain spike.

A stem rising from a round red-brown bowl- or cup-shaped base (like a pot, corm or tuber) set on four or five large pale-red heart- or turnip-shaped tubers or leaves lying flat, each with fine writing-like hatching. Six spiky green whorls of long narrow, curling, tentacle-like leaves (like octopuses or sea anemones, with olive-tipped ends) grow along the branches. At the top are three clusters of round red berries. Red berries in clusters suggest asparagus, butcher's broom, red currant, bryony, or Solomon's seal; the whorls suggest asparagus, madder or woodruff.

Five curving fronds of fan- or wedge-shaped, notched leaflets in pairs (like maidenhair fern, rue, or ginkgo-like leaflets) spread from a forked red-brown root with many rootlets. From the centre rises a tall stalk ending in a cluster of about seven dark blue round berries on short stalks, each with a small pale cap. Maidenhair fern (capillus veneris) by leaf shape, or rue; blue berries suggest bilberry, privet, elder or juniper.

Three plant panels. 94v: a dense fan of long lanceolate leaves (some blue-tinged) on a sheaf of stems, with one tall stalk bearing a single dark round flower (dark petals around a pale centre with a red eye, like an eye) on a green ribbed calyx; the roots end in four large oval tubers, two orange-brown and two dark brown/black (one marked with an X), each with a small eye. 95r1: two curving stems with many rounded leaflets in pairs (like a vetch, liquorice or chickpea), with hanging dark blue tubular flowers or pods and small red-and-white four-petalled flowers; spreading red roots. 95r2: a clump of many lanceolate leaves rising from an olive cushion- or disc-shaped base with red roots spreading beneath (like a pot, turf or cake), with about ten green capsules or acorn-like buds on stalks. Orchid (paired tubers, 'testiculus'), black and white hellebore, liquorice/vetch, leek/garlic, or a tussock sedge.

(The Yale caption reads '95v (part)', but '95' is written top right, so this may be the other side of the 95 fold-out.) A tree-like plant on a thick red-brown branching root. Pairs of oblong green leaves with fringed, curled edges (like hairy or ciliate leaves) hang on side branches. At the top a broad candelabrum of fine branching stalks carries about 50 small uncoloured round capsules, cups or berries, each with a dot (like an umbel of seed heads, or grapes). Elder, an umbellifer in seed, or a currant or vine.

Three leafy stems with deeply lobed, oak- or celery-like leaves in green and olive rise from a long horizontal red-brown rhizome with flame-like pointed lobes. Two arching sprays (left and right) and a few top stalks bear many round dark blue flowers or berries, each with a scalloped pale rim (like small blue rosettes or forget-me-not clusters). Larkspur, columbine, crane's-bill, celery or lovage in flower; blue round heads suggest scabious or sheep's-bit.

A tall pale stem with seven or eight spiky green tufts (whorls of long narrow, wavy, tentacle-like leaves, like asterisks) on side branches. A small coiled spiral knot sits on the stem. At the top is a large hooded, curved spathe-like shape (blue-grey and olive, like a hood, a cowl or an arum spathe) holding a dotted pale yellow spadix or comb, plus a green striped bulb below the hood. A pale tan root spreads into two big fan-shaped masses of roots. Arum/dragon arum (hooded spathe), monkshood (hood), asparagus or madder (whorled tufts).

Three slender green stems on a single red-brown hairy rootstock, with many alternate arrowhead- or ivy-shaped leaves (deeply notched at the base, sagittate). Long hanging clusters of small red-and-white berries or buds (like grape bunches or currant strings) dangle from the lower branches. Bindweed, black bryony, buckwheat, sheep's sorrel or arum (arrow leaves); red berries suggest black bryony, bittersweet or currant.

Pharmaceutical section. Four red cylindrical apothecary jars or boxes (albarelli or pyxides with lids) run down the left margin, each with a word written on its body as a label. Rows of small labelled drawings of roots and root pieces sit beside them: forked, curled, bulbous, hairy, segmented (one like a centipede or a caterpillar), some red-brown, some tan, one like a bird or a horned creature. At the bottom is a large hairy segmented root (like a caterpillar or a bottle brush) and a climbing vine with ivy- or arrow-shaped leaves and two small dangling red cone-like catkins or fruits. Each jar label and root label is a likely name of a drug (root) and its container.

Pharmaceutical section. Four tall red-and-white banded jars with blue tops run down the left margin, each with a label on its body. Labelled drawings of roots and root pieces sit beside them: hairy, forked, red-brown, a centipede-like segmented root, bulbous and fleshy red roots, a striped carrot or radish shape, root crowns with fringe, and a pale blue-and-white crossed object (like tongs or a cut stem). At the bottom, a large green curling leaf (like a cabbage or a dock leaf, or an elephant-ear) with a scalloped margin sits on a green stalk over long blue-green spreading roots.

Pharmaceutical section. Two red cylindrical jars at the left (top and middle). Two rows of small, separately labelled whole plants and leaves: a plant with heart-shaped leaves; a curled stem with arrow-shaped leaflets; a pinnate fern-like frond; a lobed leaf; a branching plant with leaves tipped dark blue; a two-leaved seedling; a comb-like crescent of narrow leaflets; a toothed leaf on a red root; a dark green spiky hand-shaped leaf on a red root; a palmate leaf clump; a pair of big drooping leaves. Lower row: a forked-leaf plant with a bulb; a broccoli- or cauliflower-like head on a long root; an oval toothed leaf; a round scalloped leaf; a large serrated nettle- or sage-like leaf on red roots. Each is probably a named herb (simple).

Pharmaceutical fold-out of two to three panels. A few jars (red, and blue-and-white banded) sit in the margins. Many small, separately labelled whole herbs fill the page: bushy herbs, pinnate and fern-like fronds, broad leaves, spiky leaf clusters, a feathery blue frond, small blue star-flowered sprigs, a plant with round dark-blue leaves, leafy rosettes on carrot-like roots, a tree-like plant with round crowns, and a lily- or iris-like flowering stem. They are coloured green, olive and blue; at least 40 items in all. A catalogue of medicinal herbs (simples) with names.

Pharmaceutical section. Three jars run down the left margin: a red jar with a blue top, a stacked blue-green, blue and red jar, and a red jar with a blue top. About 15 labelled whole herbs fill the page: a parsley- or celery-like bush on a horizontal root; a palm-like frond on a red carrot root; a star-shaped arrangement of arrowhead leaves on two red tubers; an ivy-leaved climber; a curled-up round leaf (like a snail or a coiled leaf); a nettle-like leaf on a forked root; a round kidney-shaped leaf on long tan roots; a thistle- or star-headed spiny plant (sea holly or caltrop) with spiky star fruits; a fern; a pinnate frond; two plants topped by dark blue cupped flowers; a fan-leaved plant; and an oak-leaved plant whose root has a small human face drawn on it (a mandrake?). A labelled catalogue of simples.

Three pharmaceutical panels. Left (101v part 2): about 20 labelled small herbs: red hanging pepper- or chili-like pods on a stem, grass blades, broad lanceolate leaves, a lily-like plant, heart-shaped leaves, round-leaved plants, a red-spiked flowering stem (like a red clover or amaranth spike), a plant with black berries, and a bulb with roots. Middle (102r1): three red jars with labels, a cut tree-stump-like root with green shoots and a hairy red root beside it, a large two-ended root or tuber lying sideways (like a ginger rhizome or a split root), and at the bottom a big red-brown mandrake-like root with round leaves beside a broad-leaved plant on a blue-green mound. Right (102r2): two jars (red, and green-banded), a red-brown octopus-like root with large leaves, a small dark blue star or flower top right, several red forked roots, a hairy-bearded root, and at the bottom a long tan worm- or caterpillar-like root with many legs (like a centipede or polypody) plus a few small red roots.

Pharmaceutical section. Two tall ornate tiered vessels run down the left margin: blue and white bands with labels written on their bodies, flared stands and finials (like turned wooden or majolica jars). Small labelled leaves and roots: an oak leaf, a fringed leaf, a small blue cube-like object (a stone, mineral or piece of something, perhaps a gem or salt), a dark blue crown- or comb-shaped object with spikes (like a coral, a cockscomb or a crown), a pale leaf with fingers, lobed and scalloped green leaves, a large serrated pinnate leaf (like dandelion or sow-thistle), a red curled pod or root, a red long carrot root, a pale-tan tangled root, a dark mushroom-like cap on a stalk, and a pale onion or bulb with roots on the right. The blue cube may represent a mineral simple (lapis lazuli, vitriol, alum).
candidates_en: mineral simple (blue stone / lapis lazuli / vitriol)

pages.description: Pharmaceutical section. Two ornate segmented jars (red and blue bands, one with a pedestal) on the left. Top row of roots with leaves: a large brown stain over a pale root crown; a round tan bulb or turnip with long thin roots under a spiky green tuft; a pale striped cup-shaped root base with red roots under broad leaves; a scaly comb-like object over a tan bearded root (like a cut rhizome with leaves). Lower row: a split tan root with two green leaves; a tan many-legged root; a dark green comb-like leaf; a large red-brown octopus-like root with a pale crown and a spiky green tuft. All labelled.

Last leaf (verso), mostly blank and stained. At the very top are three or four lines of writing in the ordinary Latin alphabet in a different hand, not the manuscript's own script, apparently mixed with a few manuscript-like letterforms. A cautious reading: line 1 'por le bon simon ...' or 'pox leber umen ...' (perhaps 'por le bon[e] ... '); line 2 '+ anchiton oladabas + ... + te + ... cere + portas + ...' (words separated by crosses, like a charm or a list of ingredients); line 3 '... + mo... + vix + ... + ...'. Some readers might see 'michiton' rather than 'anchiton'. A small faint sketch (an animal or figure?) is in the left margin. Crosses between words are typical of charms, blessings and magical formulae of the period; the content may also be a recipe, an ownership note or a pen trial.
